Hi, new Voaters and new subs to /v/mathrock! Thanks for joining and sharing some great music so far.

I dislike rules and don’t want to be a genre snob, but there are a couple of submissions that are in no way musically related to math rock, even by the broadest definitions.

Do you think we should:

  1. Leave it up to users to up/downvote submissions?

  2. Remove submissions that are clearly unrelated?

Either way feelings will be hurt if people care about their fake internet points or have wildly differing opinions of what constitutes math rock. Luckily (or not), I don’t care about your feelings, but I just want to keep the sub on-topic and relevant for math rock fans.

If submissions are removed, they will always show up in the public modlog (which is currently empty).

Please let me know what you think about this, or if you have any other feedback on the sub so far.

P.S. I know comments currently look like crap and I’ll fix it later today.

Update: I've added some basic rules and information on math rock to the sidebar. Hopefully that will do!
[meta] Please keep it mathy! (Or, do we need rules?)

I vote for #1, let the users decide. That being said, I think having a better definition of what constitutes math rock might help out a lot.

Being someone who isn't really familiar with the term, while I already submitted a link I wasn't actually sure if it fit here, haha. And after watching some of the other videos that have been submitted, I'm still not really clear on what is applicable.

Is it music with complex rhythmic structures (poly rhythm, etc.), is it things that are repetitive in nature, does complex harmony factor in it all? And is it rock specifically? I know a few jazz acts that would be potentially related.

Anyway, that's my 2 cents.

Hey! Thanks for responding.

The problem with defining a genre, there's such a range of different music that is considered math rock, I don't even know where to start. Personally I enjoy some of the '90s US scene (Don Caballero, Pele, American Football), which ranges more on the rock/jazz/emo scale... to the modern UK bands (Tubelord, Colour, TTNG, Tangled Hair) which could all easily be called "indie" bands... to Japanese bands (Toe, LITE) which don't really fall anywhere, just instrumental rock.

Complex rhythm is definitely part of it, and rock instrumentation (electric guitars, electric basses, drums) is usual but isn't that pretty much all modern Western-influenced music?

As a user I lean towards #1 myself, but as a mod it irks me that I have to leave one obviously unrelated electro track on the front page. Like c'mon, the guy who posted it must know it has nothing to do with math rock, even if they're not sure what math rock is. If I didn't know what jazz was I still wouldn't post a Taylor Swift song to /v/jazz. :)

Btw, I enjoyed the Mehliana track. First time hearing of them. Not a group I would have discovered otherwise. And jazz and jazz-fusion is definitely related! Have you heard of mouse on the keys? Think you'll like them.

I definitely understand that it can be hard to define a genre. I just think any music can be argued to be "mathematical"(all rhythm/harmony has some sort of math underlying it), so it would help to clarify just a bit. Maybe just having some version of that first paragraph in the sidebar would give people some guidance.

I personally love complex rhythm/harmony in music, so I'm looking forward to seeing what gets posted here. I'm definitely going to check out some of the bands you mentioned since I haven't heard of the vast majority of them, haha.

As for the unrelated tracks being on the front page, I think that's just a factor of voat being pretty small right now and not much content being generated. Assuming the sub grows to a decent size, the users should take care of that stuff pretty well.

Glad you liked Mehliana (the whole "Taming the Dragon" album is awesome), pretty much anything with Mark Guiliana (the drummer) is guaranteed to be on the complex side with regards to rhythm haha.

And yes, I love Mouse on the Keys. They are actually the first thing I thought of when I found this sub. :)
